findings.title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting on caught exceptions
findings.body:
The test sets `deletedAll` to true and immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty. It never joins the reader thread. A request still in flight (often the one most likely to hit a just-deleted group) can fail and append its exception after the assertion has already passed, so regressions can go undetected.

The test also never checks that the reader completed at least one request while deletions were running. If the thread starts late, the test passes without exercising the race.

If any `remove()` call throws, `deletedAll` is never set and the non-daemon thread keeps hammering the server forever. Keep a reference to the thread, set the flag in a `finally` block, `join()` it with a timeout before asserting, and ideally count the reads that overlapped the deletions.

findings.title: Same NPE remains in the other delegate-backed sub-group methods
findings.body:
The fix null-guards only `getSubGroupsCount()`. Three sibling methods still dereference `modelSupplier.get()` without a check:
- `getSubGroupsStream(search, first, max)` (line 256)
- `getSubGroupsStream(first, max)` (line 262)
- `getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, first, max)` (line 268)

When another request deletes the group between the cache lookup and these calls, the supplier returns null and these methods throw the same NPE described in #40368. That can happen when listing subgroups or searching groups. They should be guarded consistently, for example by returning `Stream.empty()` when the model is null.
